description:
cut_in_component_returns (jobs/transport.rs ~2182) asks whether the callee is in the owner's cycle group, under the derivation whose waits are Direct edges (closure-call returns skipped) or All edges; the non-rising function id tie-break is unchanged. Deletes ReachKey (Direct, All) and the Reach product entirely. On even/odd the cut must stay on odd->even. Predict: dumps identical.

PREMISE REFUTED 2026-11-14 with fz-t93.3 (scratchpad t93_3/findings.md 'H3', h1/report.md): engine cycle groups are scheduling facts that never shrink (an off-cycle member stays after an edit), so 'is the callee in the owner's cycle group' would keep cutting an edge whose cycle an edit removed. The read-graph alternative does not answer this question either: the cut needs separate Direct and All edge subsets over settled facts so every run cuts the same edges. Reach (Direct, All) stays a derived fact. Not built.

REOPENED 2026-11-14 with fz-t93.3 (plan /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-next.html): the stale-membership premise refutation depends on fz-t93.18. Experiment first, after fz-t93.18 and fz-t93.3: does the owner's (shrinking) group give the same cut edges as Reach(Direct/All) on the corpus and across edits? Buys if it holds: the Reach(Direct/All) walks are deleted.
title: The transport cut asks the engine for the owner's cycle group
